title: Recover Lost Column Auto-Advance
description:
**SITUATION:**

Forgeboard boards stall when cards sit in Doing with no owner follow-up. Product wants a small auto-advance feature: if a card stays in Doing longer than a threshold, move it to Blocked so the board stays honest for sprint reviews. You built that on `feature/column-auto-advance` and committed **Add column auto-advance for stale Doing cards** (it created `src/column_automate.py`). You had not pushed that commit yet.

Tidying up before standup, you ran git reset --hard HEAD~1 on that feature tip thinking you were cleaning a dirty tree — and the file and commit vanished from the branch. git log on the feature no longer shows it. origin still has the old feature tip without the auto-advance work.

Panic is optional; committed work is often still in the repository even when no branch tip points at it. Recover that commit onto `feature/column-auto-advance`, then push the feature so it can go to review. This work was never on `main` — leave `main` alone and do not park the rescue there. The team remote will not accept a push straight onto `main`.

You are Ada Learner in `~/sprint-service` — you start on `feature/column-auto-advance` after the accidental reset. `origin` already points at the team forge.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Figure out how to find the commit that disappeared from the feature tip.
2. Restore it so it is part of `feature/column-auto-advance` again.
3. Make sure `src/column_automate.py` is back exactly as written, and you are still on the feature branch.
4. Push `feature/column-auto-advance` to `origin` for review. Do not push or update `main`.
5. Leave everything committed with a clean working tree.

hints: git log on the feature tip will not show the lost commit — look for another way Git records where HEAD has been.
Find the SHA whose subject is Add column auto-advance for stale Doing cards, then put the feature tip back on that commit (or re-apply it).
Stay on feature/column-auto-advance. Do not switch to main to park the rescue.
After the tip is restored, push the feature to origin for review. Leave main alone.
problemStatement.overview: Forgeboard column auto-advance was committed on a private feature tip, then lost to reset --hard before push. Recover it onto the feature and push for review — leave `main` alone.
problemStatement.brief: Recover the lost column auto-advance commit on `feature/column-auto-advance`, push the branch for review. Do not park it on `main`.
problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Recover Lost Column Auto-Advance

You hard-reset away the column auto-advance commit on **feature/column-auto-advance** before it was on origin. Restore it from the reflog, then push the feature for review. Leave `main` alone.

## 1. Confirm it is gone

```bash
cd ~/sprint-service
git branch --show-current   # feature/column-auto-advance
git log --oneline           # no "Add column auto-advance for stale Doing cards"
ls src                      # no column_automate.py
```

## 2. Ask the reflog

```bash
git reflog
```

```text
79fdd2d HEAD@{0}: reset: moving to HEAD~1
1102836 HEAD@{1}: commit: Add column auto-advance for stale Doing cards
...
```

HEAD@{1} is the lost commit.

## 3. Restore it on the feature

```bash
git reset --hard <lost-sha>
# or: git cherry-pick <lost-sha>
```

Stay on feature/column-auto-advance.

## 4. Push for review

```bash
git push -u origin feature/column-auto-advance
git log --oneline
cat src/column_automate.py
git status
```

Do not push main.

## Takeaways

- reset --hard moves a private tip. Recover locally first; origin only learns after you push.
- The reflog is a local safety net — not shared with the remote.
